chapter: Follow-up questions, Bird and the Ellington sidemen
title: After Stuff: 52nd Street trio with Ray Perry and the Onyx reviews
summary: Clubowners paired Jones, John Levy and violinist Ray Perry; the Chicago reputation brought critics to the Onyx.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: You and John, after you left Stuff Smith, what all were you doing? I know you said you had a duo and just went everywhere, but where was everywhere?
Well, it was mainly on 52nd Street.
And you worked with Ben then and who else?
Don Byas, Ben, and with the same Ray Perry I just spoke about. He was playing jazz violin, and when Stuff started acting up, you know, so the clubowners put us together.
So it was a trio, you and John and Ray Perry.
There was no leader. They just put us
You also mentioned that you said, I think off the tape, that Stuff changed a lot when he got to New York.

Yeah, he didn't mean to. He just got carried away, because we had made quite a reputation in Chicago, at the Garrick Lounge, and had so many good writeups, so as soon as we got to New York everybody was in the Onyx, all the critics, and we got great reviews, and that really launched me and it launched John, you know?
And that's when John sent for the rest of his family because he wasn't going back to Chicago either. We just saw -- that was the marketplace at that time, that was the place to be, you know?
